result.topic_en: Gauss takes a quantity as constant, derives a pair of second-order differential equations in T and U, and finds a first integral by multiplying by $UT'-TU'$. He then substitutes $T=p^{-2}$ and manipulates the resulting equations in p, q, r; faint pencil calculations appear on the right.
result.transcription:
Setzt man anstatt $2\xi$ [?], $de^{\xi}$ [?] constant so werden die Gleichungen
$0=\frac{UU-TT}{TU^4}+4T''$
$0=\frac{UU-TT}{UT^4}-4U''$
also
$4UT''-4TU''+\frac{U^4-T^4}{T^3U^3}=0$
Diese wird Integrabel wenn man mit $UT'-TU'$ multipl.
$2(UT'-TU')^2=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{TT}{UU}+\frac{UU}{TT}\right)+\text{Const.}$
Die Constante findet sich $=-1$
